# Claude Code 2.1.318: editor-probe, freshness, M59 and parser-cost evidence

Measured on 2026-11-04 for PRD #1666 part 3's activation, on the executable with SHA-256 `708c77b204db30086ff6f1ed34577bda03e1be74ced80557cbf7b54249ebf0bd`: the official `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.318` (tarball integrity `sha512-GX+7CUng2R5f7SsA2w0LaXlH2f62fRCFD/Z2SUexoeH3B0KfulKQt5DtY9NeD2Yp3VEBz6/k/xWSbGPUi6NV2A==`, matching the registry's), byte-identical to the copy the host's installer put in `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.318` on 2026-11-04. That copy was pinned to private scratch space outside the checkout and reached through a private `claude` symlink; the host's own Claude config was never used. The screen and ring captures for the same release are under `../r5wake/` (`claude-2.1.318-*`, described in `../r5wake/claude-menu-candidates.md`, sections "Claude Code 2.1.318" and "History recall"). The editor-probe, M59 and freshness runs here were local lane-2 runs, in the TUI harness's own HOME, with every submission blocked by a private hook before a model turn. `parser-cost-replay.txt` is not a lane-2 run: it is the output of an `--ignored` unit replay in the release profile over the recorded traces, these included, run in this worktree's RWX sandbox (16 cores; load average 6.52 at its start, from the sandbox's own build).

## Recorders, and how the summaries are made

Each recorder is `tests/support/claude_editor_measure.py` (editor probe) or `tests/support/claude_helper_alarm_measure.py` (M59), and each summary's `recorder_sha256` is that of the committed file: `b3fa8073…` and `a11e7747…` are the revisions 2.1.317's summaries were made with (`2a4ccb92…`, `bbacdcc3…`) plus one line each, the 2.1.318 entry in their SHA-256 pin map. Every summary was written by `tests/support/claude_evidence_summary.py` from its capture's `result.json`, whose docstring gives the field mapping; `python3 -I tests/support/claude_evidence_summary.py --check <source_capture> <summary>` regenerates one and compares it byte for byte. The test bodies are the ones 2.1.317 ran: each `probe_08x_live_claude_317_*` and `probe_090_live_claude_317_*` test now calls a body that takes the release, and its `…_318_…` twin calls the same body with `2.1.318`, so every assertion 2.1.317's run made was made on 2.1.318 too.

## What 2.1.318 measured, against 2.1.317

No reading differs from 2.1.317 on any value a record or an `EditorProbe` would take.

- **Export, selection, paste toggles.** 5/5 `VISUAL` presses handed the editor the draft in `/tmp/claude-1000/claude-prompt-<uuid>.md` (`TMPDIR` unset) as its last argument and reimported the rewritten file; an empty `VISUAL` fell to `EDITOR`; with neither, PATH `code` (run as `code -w -g <file>:1`) before `vi` (`vi +1 <file>`). The `VISUAL` path wrote one `?2004l` before the editor and one `?2004h` after it, 5/5, asserted as that value; `EDITOR` and PATH `vi` wrote the same, and the PATH `code -w -g` fallback wrote none. The editor exiting 37 kept the draft.
- **Keymap sources and P-KB1 (M49b).** The unbinding file present at spawn was in force at the first composer frame 5/5 (first composer 1.05–1.41 s after spawn): Ctrl+G inert, Ctrl+E opened. Unchanged for ten minutes: Ctrl+G inert 10/10, stat unchanged 10/10, Ctrl+E still opened. Created during a session it took effect by 3.65 s, removed by 3.87 s (sampled times, not a race bound). The same file in the project's `.claude/` had no effect, with user settings only and with every settings source.
- **M44e forms.** All 73 state/form cells read as 2.1.317's, cell for cell: BEL, implicit CSI-u 103/71 and modifyOtherKeys 103/71 open the editor in the draft, slash, help, shell-mode and after-Escape-twice states (10/12 each), reverse search swallows every form, explicit-event CSI-u never opens it, and contiguous ESC BEL never does. ESC then BEL opened it at a 60 ms gap and not at 0 or 30 ms, as on 2.1.317.
- **Pasted BEL: kept as text.** A bracketed `PASTE` BEL `TAIL` opened no editor, whole and split, and the next export held `BASEPASTE\x07TAIL`, read from the bytes the editor stand-in read from the file (the screen draws no BEL, so it reads `BASEPASTETAIL` either way). `probe_089` asserts that reading. The proposed record value stays `Absent`, as 2.1.317's.
- **M59, 31 trials, all pass.** Cell (a), armed and stalled at the first ready poll: no editor in 10/10, the draft kept, the helper's trace ending at `pause ready` with no orderly exit, the helper ending 5.0018–5.0066 s after its branch, and SIGALRM seen directly in 10/10 by Claude's own notice `… closed unexpectedly (SIGALRM)` written after the helper's end (the zombie's wait status 0/10). Row T, armed with an unanswered exchange (not an alarm pass): `armed None ArmedExit { notice: true, status: 0 }` 10/10, the helper's notice on the terminal 10/10, ended 3.514–3.519 s after its branch. Cell (b), unarmed: one editor run each, the helper alive 10.11–10.16 s, `exit Status(0)` 10/10 with the sentinel reimported, then `exit Status(37)` on the eleventh press with Claude's `quit unexpectedly (exit code 37)` and the draft kept; the zombie was seen once, exited 0.
- **Parser cost.** 2.1.318's traces at most 87.5 µs added to a push's lock hold and 3.39 ms of scanner CPU per generation. Over every trace in this run (n = 417 510 pushes at 50×200 and 80×300): aggregate added-hold p99 66.1 µs, at most 292.1 µs, at most 3.86 ms CPU per generation, no work limit reached; every trace's own p99 and maximum, and every generation's CPU, within plan §4.6's limits (146 per-trace rows checked). This run is on the RWX sandbox, not on the box 2.1.317's replay ran on (load 10.65 on 16 CPUs there), so its figures are not comparable with that file's; in this run 2.1.317's traces reached at most 92.8 µs and 3.20 ms, and 2.1.312's 147.9 µs and 3.57 ms.

## A-20d-7 on a throwaway build

The `e2e` build's editor-probe assumption refuses a release with no record of its own, so `probe_083` ran on a local build of part 3 at `aa1d34ed` with one uncommitted change: a 2.1.318 `RELEASE_RECORDS` entry holding 2.1.317's values (its `editor_probe` left `Absent`, as 2.1.317's is). That build was never committed and its worktree is removed; `build_id` in each line names it (`-dirty`). These lines are provisional and informational, and the gate's evidence is the rerun against a committed 2.1.318 record.

Five runs on 2026-11-04 (`DOT_AGENT_DECK_REQUIRE_REAL_E2E=1`, the pinned executable above via `DAD_PROBE_FRESHNESS_BINARY`), all five passing; `build_id` `0.49.5-gaa1d34ed-dirty` on every line. Of 350 probes outside the control, none was refused for freshness at the writer and none when scheduled, and every one was written: per run, 40 at the production interval (round trip at most 15 ms), 15 held 100 ms and 15 held 1 s. The control refused 25 of 25 for freshness. The idle agent drew one 43-byte frame per minute's watch and no frame between probes, in every run. Contention, read from each line's own fields: 1-minute load 1.1–2.2 at the idle runs (15-minute 4.0–6.1) and 17.5 and 19.3 under the sixteen burners, CPU pressure (`some avg10`) at most 0.72% idle and 6.4% and 12.8% under the burners. This matches 2.1.317's provisional and committed-record lines. The uncommitted change is kept as a diff at `/var/tmp/dad-t318-claude-2.1.318/proposed-record.diff` on the recording machine.
